text:
Mason Marchment has been one of the unluckier forwards in the league. The Sharks have scored 7.5 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and it has cost him: seven points in 19 games for a player who had 45 last season. Our numbers flag him as due, and this is the kind of gap that usually closes.

He's on his sixth NHL team after going undrafted, and his role has grown since Alexander Wennberg went down. He moved onto the first power-play unit and plays beside Tyler Toffoli, and Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest singled out a back-door pass to Will Smith on Saturday. He's one goal from 100 for his career.

The value isn't only offensive. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.5 wins last season, and their adjusted numbers showed opponents getting fewer chances with him on the ice (85th percentile). He isn't fast, by NHL Edge his top speed sits near the bottom tenth of the league, but he gets to good spots. Our range has him at 35 to 56 points over a full season. Expect the points to arrive in bunches once the bounces even out.
headline: Marchment's luck should turn
